Chapter VI · Unit 148

Translates of Poincaré series fill the rows: a Petersson-type second moment along a Bessel subgroup

note and structured proofs · 496 declarations · 179 structured proofs · 8 notes

Unit 148 (the folder New/Filling) proves the filling theorem used for Theorem B (enough forms): for admissible data D, every nonzero constant c and every subspace F of the rows, some element s of the finite level group 𝖦 = ∏ GL over the residue fields at the chosen places above g = q₀q₁ makes the preimage of F under the composite (|𝖦| e₀ s) ∘ 𝒫 ∘ (c·E) have dimension at most ((1 + dim F/dim rows)/2 + b⁻²)·dim Col, where 𝒫 is the Poincaré series built from cut Bessel functions along the Bessel subgroup S = 𝖴𝖧 of the unitary group of V = H^ϱ ⊕ X₀ ⊕ Ez, e₀ the projection to the rows and E the projection onto the ramified columns (Data.ramifiedColumns_fill_rows). The proof is a second-moment (Petersson-type) argument: the mean over s of the squared Hilbert–Schmidt norm of 𝒫*s𝒫 is unfolded into sums of amplitudes over rational elements γ grouped by double cosets (classes c, c') and by their reductions s modulo g; amplitude sums vanish unless the unipotent characters agree, degenerate terms and incoherent pairs are negligible by discriminant gains, lattice counts and a weighted Schur test, the main term is bounded nearly sharply by positive kernels of local Bessel integrals at finitely many places and a sieve (one-sided Poisson summation), and a variance inequality turns the moment bound into the spreading statement. Chunk 148-a holds the set-up and the first layer: the record Filling of the data and its standing hypotheses IsAdmissible; abstract sieve systems and Bessel systems; the groups 𝖴, 𝖴⁰, 𝖧, 𝖲, the classes, terms, amplitudes and constants; dictionaries between rational, finite adelic and real coordinates; links of frames (Lagrangian, invariant under 𝖴 on both sides); Siegel's lemma for hermitian lattices and a convergent height zeta function of subspaces; strong approximation for 𝖴; normal forms and levels of terms; the bound of the index of a determinant of pairings by agreeing characters; box partitions (cutoffs) for the arithmetic unipotent groups 𝖴_c(g) and the frame-counting bound; the exact covolume of 𝖴_c(g); and convergence, change of weight, moves, vanishing for disagreeing characters and the identity term of the amplitude sums.
